registry_objects.title: Right-handed decoupling
registry_objects.summary: Corollary of the Chirality Selection Theorem: for any right-handed configuration psi_R in Gamma_R, all polarity-switching amplitudes vanish identically: <chi_{-epsilon} | Phi_A | psi_R> = 0 for all epsilon; right-handed configurations are weak-interaction singlets.

registry_objects.title: Twin Prime Residue Theorem
registry_objects.summary: The S₅ correction 121/120 is DERIVED via twin prime residue: for (p,q)=(3,5) twin primes with a=pq-p-1=11, s=(p-1)(q-1)=8, n=pq=15, the identity a²=s·n+1 holds because p(q-1)(q-p-2)=0. Upgraded from conjectural (was IV.C02 E₁ Page Hypothesis).

registry_objects.title: Sector Physics Template
registry_objects.summary: Four defining parameters for each sector at E₁: self-coupling κ(S;d) as rational function of ι_τ, polarity signature (χ₊-dom/balanced/χ₋-dom/crossing), primorial depth d ∈ {1,2,3}, and kernel generator. Also defines PolaritySign inductive type.

registry_objects.title: EM Sector at E₁
registry_objects.summary: B-sector instantiation: γ-generator, self-coupling κ(B;2) = ι_τ², χ₊-dominant polarity, depth 2. Physical: photon transport, Maxwell equations, fine structure constant.

registry_objects.title: Strong Sector at E₁
registry_objects.summary: C-sector instantiation: η-generator, self-coupling κ(C;3) = ι_τ³/(1−ι_τ), χ₋-dominant polarity, depth 3. The (1−ι_τ) denominator is the structural signature of confinement.

registry_objects.title: Higgs Sector at E₁
registry_objects.summary: ω-sector instantiation: γ∩η crossing generator, self-coupling κ(B,C) = ι_τ³/(1+ι_τ), crossing polarity, depth 3. Unique +1 derived sector from the lemniscate crossing point. Physical: mass generation.

registry_objects.title: Gravity Sector at E₁
registry_objects.summary: D-sector instantiation: α-generator, self-coupling κ(D;1) = 1−ι_τ, χ₊-dominant polarity, depth 1. Temporal sector on base τ¹. Physical: frame holonomy, gravitational constant G = (c³/ℏ)·ι_τ².

registry_objects.title: Weak Sector at E₁
registry_objects.summary: A-sector instantiation: π-generator, self-coupling κ(A;1) = ι_τ, balanced polarity (unique), depth 1. The master constant ι_τ itself IS the weak self-coupling. Physical: temporal arrow, parity violation, beta decay.

registry_objects.title: Coupling Formula Map
registry_objects.summary: All 10 inter-sector couplings as rational functions of ι_τ. 4 self-couplings: κ(D)=1−ι_τ, κ(A)=ι_τ, κ(B)=ι_τ², κ(C)=ι_τ³/(1−ι_τ). 6 cross-couplings: electroweak, weak-strong, weak-gravity, EM-strong, EM-gravity, strong-gravity. Complete 10-entry coupling ledger.

registry_objects.title: Spectral Fine Structure
registry_objects.summary: Spectral fine structure constant α ≈ (8/15)·ι_τ⁴. Leading-order approximation from two τ² surface modes (exponent 4) and primorial factor 8/15 = 2³/(3·5). Gives α ≈ 0.00725, 1/α ≈ 137.9 (spectral approx, ~0.06% from experiment).

registry_objects.title: Primary Invariant
registry_objects.summary: The 5 primary physical invariants: Entropy, Time, Energy, Mass, Gravity. These exhaust the independent physical degrees of freedom; all derived from ι_τ via sector lifts.

registry_objects.title: Carrier Type
registry_objects.summary: Carrier type for physical quantities in τ³ = τ¹ ×_f T²: Fiber (T², microcosm), Base (τ¹, macrocosm), or Crossing (lemniscate point).

registry_objects.title: Electromagnetic Field Tensor
registry_objects.summary: The electromagnetic field tensor (Faraday 2-form) is the curvature F = dA of the EM connection, with components F_mu_nu = partial_mu A_nu - partial_nu A_mu.

registry_objects.title: Electric and Magnetic Field Extraction
registry_objects.summary: Electric field E_i = F_0i and magnetic field B_i = (1/2)*epsilon_ijk*F_jk extracted from the field tensor by temporal-spatial decomposition.

registry_objects.title: Hodge Dual of F
registry_objects.summary: The Hodge dual (*F)_mu_nu = (1/2)*epsilon_mu_nu_rho_sigma*F^rho_sigma implements electric-magnetic duality: E -> B, B -> -E.

registry_objects.title: Electromagnetic Current 4-Vector
registry_objects.summary: The EM current 4-vector J^mu = sum_a q_a n_a u_a^mu is the B-sector component of the total defect density, with charges from U(1) winding numbers.

registry_objects.title: tau-Native Fine-Structure Constant
registry_objects.summary: The tau-native fine-structure constant alpha_tau is the ratio of the minimal AB holonomy on T_gamma to the photon phase quantum from tau^1, involving only tau^3-intrinsic objects.

registry_objects.title: Null Transport Mode
registry_objects.summary: A null transport mode on tau^1 propagates with vanishing net fiber holonomy in both gamma and eta directions: no electric or color charge.

registry_objects.title: Holonomy Correction Factor
registry_objects.summary: The holonomy correction factor R(iota_tau) = alpha_em/alpha_spec = (15/8)*alpha_em/iota_tau^4 ~ 1.006 encodes the 0.6% refinement from fiber curvature and base-fiber coupling.

registry_objects.title: Sector Polarity
registry_objects.summary: Polarity index pol(X) measuring relative weight of chi_+ and chi_- in a sector; balanced polarity (pol=0) vs definite polarity (pol>0).

registry_objects.title: Polarity-Preserving Interaction
registry_objects.summary: An interaction that commutes with bipolar projections P_pm, mapping chi_+ to chi_+ and chi_- to chi_-.

registry_objects.title: Channel-Switching Defect Bundle
registry_objects.summary: Localised transient configuration in H_partial[omega] mediating polarity-switching: concentrated near crossing point, sector-restricted to A, carries net chi_+/chi_- difference.

registry_objects.title: Physical Quantity Template
registry_objects.summary: Physical quantity template: name, primary invariant, carrier type, governing sector, σ-fixed flag, conservation flag. All 5 canonical quantities instantiated.

registry_objects.title: W-pm Defect Bundles
registry_objects.summary: Charged channel-switching configurations on L: W- maps chi_- to chi_+, W+ maps chi_+ to chi_-. Carry electric charge pm e with mass M_W ~ 80.4 GeV from crossing tension.

registry_objects.title: Z0 Defect Bundle
registry_objects.summary: Neutral channel-switching configuration on L: probes polarity structure without changing lobe assignment. Couples to all fermions. Mass M_Z ~ 91.2 GeV exceeds M_W.

registry_objects.title: Chirality
registry_objects.summary: Eigenvalue of chirality operator gamma_5 = J circ sigma_V on spinor configurations: +1 for right-handed (Gamma_R), -1 for left-handed (Gamma_L).

registry_objects.title: A-Sector Sigma-Admissibility
registry_objects.summary: Configuration psi is sigma_A-admissible if sigma_A(psi) ~_coh psi: coherence-compatible polarity reversal restricted to the A-sector.

registry_objects.title: Parity Operator
registry_objects.summary: Spatial inversion P: (x,t) -> (-x,t) interchanging Gamma_L and Gamma_R. A process is parity-invariant if its amplitude is unchanged under P.

registry_objects.title: Crossing-Point Action Space
registry_objects.summary: The crossing-point action space V_A := C^2 carrying the natural action of the pi-generator on two-component boundary values at x_0 in L.

registry_objects.title: Weak Isospin Generators
registry_objects.summary: T_i := (1/2) sigma_i (Pauli matrices). T_3 measures lobe eigenvalue (isospin projection), T_1 and T_2 exchange lobes (polarity-switching), T_pm = T_1 pm iT_2 are raising/lowering operators.

registry_objects.title: Left-Handed Doublets
registry_objects.summary: Left-handed fermions form SU(2)_L doublets: three lepton doublets (nu_e/e, nu_mu/mu, nu_tau/tau) and three quark doublets (u/d, c/s, t/b). Upper has I_3=+1/2 (L+), lower has I_3=-1/2 (L-).

registry_objects.title: Weak Gauge Bosons Before Mixing
registry_objects.summary: The adjoint representation of SU(2)_L gives three gauge fields W^1_mu, W^2_mu, W^3_mu, one per generator T_i.

registry_objects.title: Weak Holonomy Loop
registry_objects.summary: The canonical SU(2) holonomy loop ell_A on the A-sector fibre: Hol(ell_A) = exp(ig oint W^a T_a dx) in SU(2), with coupling g determined by kappa(A;1)=iota_tau.

registry_objects.title: Particle Kind
registry_objects.summary: Particle classification: Ontic (persistent T² defect bundle), Radiation (null S¹ transport), Virtual (intermediate exchange). Neutron = first ontic particle.

registry_objects.title: W Boson Parameters
registry_objects.summary: Observed W boson: M_W = 80.377 pm 0.012 GeV, charge pm e, spin 1, width 2.085 GeV, lifetime ~3e-25 s, 3 polarizations. Charge from isospin T_pm, spin-1 from gauge connection (1-form).

registry_objects.title: Weinberg Angle from Tau-Couplings
registry_objects.summary: sin^2(theta_W) ~ kappa(A,D) = iota_tau(1-iota_tau) ~ 0.2249. Sits between PDG on-shell (0.2229) and MSbar at Z-pole (0.2312), residual 1-3% from regime-readout corrections.

registry_objects.title: Z Boson Parameters
registry_objects.summary: Observed Z boson: M_Z = 91.1876 pm 0.0021 GeV, charge 0, spin 1, width 2.4952 GeV, lifetime ~2.6e-25 s. Couples to all fermions (both L and R) via hypercharge component.

registry_objects.title: The Rho Parameter
registry_objects.summary: Electroweak rho parameter: rho := M_W^2 / (M_Z^2 cos^2(theta_W)).

registry_objects.title: Neutrino as Time-Eigenmode
registry_objects.summary: A neutrino is an eigenmode of T that is fiber-decoupled: T nu = mu nu (nontrivial temporal propagation), B nu = 0 at leading order (no fiber breathing), mass only through fiber-base coupling integral.

registry_objects.title: Neutrino Flavor Eigenstates
registry_objects.summary: Three flavor eigenstates: nu_e = fundamental eigenmode of T_pi (A-sector), nu_mu = of T_gamma (B-sector), nu_tau = of T_eta (C-sector). Each carries parent sector quantum numbers.

registry_objects.title: PMNS Matrix
registry_objects.summary: Unitary PMNS matrix U connecting flavor and mass eigenstates. Parametrized by three mixing angles theta_12, theta_23, theta_13 and one CP-violating phase delta_CP.

registry_objects.title: τ-Hypercharge
registry_objects.summary: τ-hypercharge Y := 2(Q - T_3), derived as an accounting device from EM holonomy eigenvalue Q and weak isospin T_3, not a new fundamental quantum number.

registry_objects.title: Pre-Mixing Electroweak Gauge Group
registry_objects.summary: Pre-mixing electroweak gauge group G_EW = SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y with four gauge bosons W^1, W^2, W^3 (from Sector A) and B (from Sector B).

registry_objects.title: Charged W Bosons
registry_objects.summary: Physical charged weak bosons W^± = (W^1 ∓ iW^2)/√2, mass eigenstates at ~80.4 GeV with charge ±1, determined entirely by SU(2)_L algebra without mixing angle.

registry_objects.title: Planck Character
registry_objects.summary: ℏ_τ = Lift_QM(ι_τ): universal lower bound in H_∂[ω]. σ-fixed (crossing point), attained minimum (not infimum). The QM sector lift of the master constant.

registry_objects.title: Weinberg Angle
registry_objects.summary: Weinberg (weak mixing) angle θ_W defined by tan θ_W = g'/g, where g is the SU(2)_L coupling and g' is the U(1)_Y coupling constant.

registry_objects.title: Mixing Compatibility
registry_objects.summary: Two primitive sectors are mixing-compatible iff they satisfy: (M1) shared geometric substrate, (M2) overlapping polarity channels covering both χ_+ and χ_−, (M3) complementary gauge structure (one abelian, one non-abelian).

registry_objects.title: Electroweak Coherence State
registry_objects.summary: Configuration of A∪B sectors where neutral-boson mixing matrix is maximally off-diagonal: θ_W not yet resolved, W^3 and B indistinguishable as mass eigenstates. Corresponds to T ≫ M_W regime.

registry_objects.title: Coherence Fixing (Ch33)
registry_objects.summary: Process by which crossing-point element ω resolves the A∪B coherence state into distinct mass eigenstates: mixing matrix diagonalizes, W±/Z^0 acquire mass, photon remains massless.

registry_objects.title: Coherence Fixing (Formal)
registry_objects.summary: Mechanism at crossing point p_ω that: (1) selects definite vacuum orientation in degenerate ground-state space, (2) separates EM from Strong at vacuum level, (3) stabilizes vacuum as strict local minimum. Surviving excitation is the τ-Higgs mode.

registry_objects.title: Finite-Stage Coherence Functional
registry_objects.summary: At refinement tower stage n, coherence functional V_n: Ω_n → ℝ with gradient-plus-quartic form V_n(ω_n) = ||∂_ω χ_n||² + λ_n(||χ_n||² − v_n²)². Mexican-hat structure emerges from coherence kernel, not postulated.

registry_objects.title: Physical Vacuum Ω*[ω]
registry_objects.summary: Physical vacuum at crossing point Ω*[ω] = lim←_n ω_n*, the projective limit of finite-stage minimizers compatible with the refinement tower.

registry_objects.title: Minimality Condition
registry_objects.summary: The ω-sector mode Ω*[ω] satisfies minimality if it is the simplest mode (fewest internal degrees of freedom) compatible with coherence fixing at crossing point p_ω.

registry_objects.title: EM-Nullity Condition
registry_objects.summary: The ω-sector mode satisfies EM-nullity if electrically neutral: Q_em[Ω*[ω]] = 0. Required because a charged mode would couple preferentially to Sector B, violating the mediating role.

registry_objects.title: σ-Polarity Condition
registry_objects.summary: The ω-sector mode satisfies σ-polarity if fixed by lemniscate involution σ: σ(Ω*[ω]) = Ω*[ω]. Required because vacuum is σ-invariant and excitation must not distinguish the two lobes.

registry_objects.title: Uncertainty Product
registry_objects.summary: Uncertainty product Δx·Δp template. Arises from incompatible address constraints in τ-NF, not measurement disturbance. τ-Heisenberg: Δx·Δp ≥ ℏ_τ.

registry_objects.title: Vacuum Hessian at Crossing Point
registry_objects.summary: Second variation of coherence functional about physical vacuum: H_ω = δ²V/δω² evaluated at Ω*[ω], acting on transverse fluctuations.

registry_objects.title: τ-Higgs Mass
registry_objects.summary: τ-Higgs mass defined as M_H² = λ_1 · ℏ_τ², where λ_1 is the limiting Hessian eigenvalue and ℏ_τ is the Planck character.

registry_objects.title: τ-Yukawa Coupling (Ch34)
registry_objects.summary: τ-Yukawa coupling y_τ(f) = ∂m_breathing(f)/∂v_ω: defect-sensitivity of breathing mass to coherence-fixing amplitude. Derived quantity, not a free parameter.

registry_objects.title: τ-Yukawa Coupling (Overlap Integral)
registry_objects.summary: τ-Yukawa coupling y_f^(τ) = ⟨ψ_f|Ω*[ω]|ψ_f⟩/⟨ψ_n|Ω*[ω]|ψ_n⟩: ratio of fermion f breathing-mode overlap with coherence-fixing vacuum to neutron ground-mode overlap. Determined by fibre winding numbers, crossing proximity, solenoidal count.

registry_objects.title: The C-sector
registry_objects.summary: The C-sector is the E1 instantiation of the eta-generator with primorial depth d=3, chi_minus-dominant polarity, fiber T^2 carrier, and self-coupling kappa(C;3) = iota_tau^3/(1-iota_tau), defining the strong force sector.

registry_objects.title: Strong loop class
registry_objects.summary: The strong loop class L_s[n] at primorial stage n is the subset of loops in the boundary holonomy algebra H_partial[n] satisfying eta-support, gap-class membership, and nonzero contraction defect conditions.

registry_objects.title: Strong holonomy defect
registry_objects.summary: The strong holonomy defect HolDef_{s,n}(f;ell) measures the norm difference between the holonomy of f composed with a gap loop ell and the holonomy of ell alone, quantifying how much an endomorphism distorts a single gap loop.

registry_objects.title: Strong defect functional
registry_objects.summary: The strong defect functional Delta_n^s(f) is the NFMin-aggregated minimum of holonomy defects over all gap loops in L_s[n], measuring the minimal holonomy distortion that endomorphism f inflicts on the gap-loop structure at stage n.

registry_objects.title: Strong admissibility
registry_objects.summary: An endomorphism f in S_n is strongly admissible at stage n if it preserves the eta-sector chi_minus character decomposition (SA-i), respects gap-class loops (SA-ii), and is boundary-coherent with the refinement projection (SA-iii).

registry_objects.title: Finite-stage strong vacuum
registry_objects.summary: The finite-stage strong vacuum Gamma_s^*[n] is the argmin of Delta_n^s over Adm_s[n], with NFMin tie-breaking among minimizers; it is the unique canonical ground state of the strong sector at primorial stage n.

registry_objects.title: Sector Lift Functor
registry_objects.summary: Sector lift functor Lift_S: H_fix[ω] → H_fix[ω]. Ring homomorphism, σ-equivariant. 5 canonical lifts: EM=ι_τ², Weak=ι_τ, Strong=ι_τ³/(1−ι_τ), Gravity=1−ι_τ, Higgs=ι_τ³/(1+ι_τ).

registry_objects.title: Strong vacuum
registry_objects.summary: The strong vacuum Gamma_s^* is the omega-limit (projective limit) of the finite-stage strong vacua Gamma_s^*[n] over n >= 3, taken in the category of pro-objects of the boundary holonomy algebra.

registry_objects.title: \mathrm{HolEnd_τ(s)
registry_objects.summary: HolEnd_tau(s)[n] is the space of strong-admissible boundary endomorphisms at stage n satisfying vacuum preservation (H-i), holonomy compatibility (H-ii), and boundary coherence (H-iii) within the eta-sector of the boundary holonomy algebra.

registry_objects.title: Fix(s)
registry_objects.summary: Fix(s)[n] is the fixed-point subobject of HolEnd_tau(s)[n] consisting of endomorphisms that commute with the strong vacuum: f in HolEnd_tau(s)[n] such that f composed with Gamma_s^*[n] equals Gamma_s^*[n] composed with f.

registry_objects.title: Canonical strong lift
registry_objects.summary: The canonical strong lift Lift_{s,n} is the NFMin-minimal element of HolEnd_tau(s)[n] achieving the same defect value as the strong vacuum; its omega-limit Lift_s = varprojlim Lift_{s,n} is the simplest non-trivial strong-sector endomorphism.

registry_objects.title: Color Charge
registry_objects.summary: Color charge of a character mode chi_{m,n} on T^2 is the holonomy class c(chi_{m,n}) := n mod 3 in Z/3Z = {0,1,2}, conventionally labeled red (0), green (1), blue (2), determined by the eta-winding number.

registry_objects.title: Anti-Color
registry_objects.summary: The anti-color of a mode with color class c = n mod 3 is the conjugate class c_bar := (-n) mod 3 = (3-c) mod 3, with holonomy phase omega_3^{-n} = bar{omega_3}^n, the complex conjugate of the color phase.

registry_objects.title: Color Neutrality
registry_objects.summary: A composite mode or collection of modes is color-neutral (color singlet) if the total eta-holonomy is trivial: sum_i n_i equiv 0 mod 3, where n_i is the eta-winding number of the i-th constituent.

registry_objects.title: Wilson Loop
registry_objects.summary: The Wilson loop W(gamma) = (1/3) Tr U(gamma) is the gauge-invariant trace of the holonomy around a closed path gamma, serving as the order parameter for confinement: area-law decay signals the confining phase.

registry_objects.title: Fractional CR-sublattice
registry_objects.summary: The fractional CR-sublattice Lambda_CR^{1/3} := {(m, n/3) : m,n in Z} subset Z x (1/3)Z refines the character lattice to accommodate color-charged modes with fractional eta-component n/3 not in Z.

registry_objects.title: Color-confined mode
registry_objects.summary: A mode chi_{m,n} on T^2 is color-confined if n is not equiv 0 mod 3 (fractional eta-holonomy) and the associated boundary character fails to converge in H_partial[omega] as refinement stage N tends to infinity.

registry_objects.title: Defect Component
registry_objects.summary: 4 canonical defect components: Mobility (transport), Vorticity (circulation), Compression (divergence), Topological (winding). Computed on clopen adjacency graphs.

registry_objects.title: Color singlet
registry_objects.summary: A composite state Psi is a color singlet if its total eta-holonomy is trivial: hol_eta(Psi) = 1, equivalently sum_j c_j equiv 0 mod 3, where c_j are the color charges of the constituents.

registry_objects.title: Baryon number
registry_objects.summary: Baryon number B(Psi) := (1/3) sum_j n_j is the total net eta-winding divided by 3, where n_j is the eta-winding of constituent psi_j; for a baryon with {c_1,c_2,c_3} = {0,1,2}, B = 1.

registry_objects.title: τ-Holonomy sector
registry_objects.summary: A tau-holonomy sector S consists at each finite stage n of a finite configuration space C_n (NF-enumerable), a finite admissible subset C_n^{adm} (polarity/boundary-coherent), a defect functional V_n to alpha-Idx, and surjective refinement projections.

registry_objects.title: Canonical vacuum at stage~n
registry_objects.summary: The canonical vacuum at stage n is Omega_n^* := argmin over C_n^{adm} of the lexicographic pair (V_n(Omega), code_n(Omega)), first minimizing the defect functional V_n, then tie-breaking by the smallest NF code.

registry_objects.title: Localized perturbations
registry_objects.summary: The localized perturbation set P_n(U) is the set of admissible perturbations p in C_n^{adm} supported within a region U subset T^2 such that the superposition Omega_n^* oplus p remains admissible.

registry_objects.title: Finite-difference quadratic form
registry_objects.summary: The finite-difference quadratic form Q_n(p,q) := V_n(Omega^* oplus p oplus q) - V_n(Omega^* oplus p) - V_n(Omega^* oplus q) + V_n(Omega^*) measures the second-order excitation cost around the canonical vacuum.

registry_objects.title: Excitation cost
registry_objects.summary: The excitation cost lambda_n(p) := (Q_n(p,p), ||p||_n) is the lexicographic pair of the quadratic energy cost and the NF-norm, measuring how energetically expensive a perturbation is above the vacuum with degeneracy-breaking.

registry_objects.title: Canonical smallest excitation
registry_objects.summary: The canonical smallest excitation h_n is the lexicographic argmin of (lambda_n(p), code_n(p)) over all nontrivial localized perturbations p in P_n(U)\{0}, representing the lightest possible excitation above the vacuum at stage n.

registry_objects.title: Three kernel hypotheses
registry_objects.summary: The three kernel hypotheses for a tau-holonomy sector are: (KH-1) eventual stationarity of combinatorial type beyond a stabilization horizon n_*, (KH-2) refinement monotonicity of the defect functional, and (KH-3) strict positivity of Q_n(p,p) for all nontrivial p.

registry_objects.title: Strong configuration space
registry_objects.summary: The strong configuration space C_s[n] = Adm_s[n] / ~_{Gamma_s^*[n]} is the quotient of strongly admissible endomorphisms at stage n by the equivalence relation induced by the canonical strong vacuum, forming the space over which the mass gap is analyzed.

registry_objects.title: Defect Tuple
registry_objects.summary: 4-component defect tuple: (mobility, vorticity, compression, topological). Universal regime classifier and regularity driver for fluid dynamics.

registry_objects.title: Strong connection assignment
registry_objects.summary: A strong connection assignment at stage n is a map Gamma_n: E(C_s[n]) -> Aut(T_n^col) assigning to each edge of the finite cell complex an automorphism of the color phase fiber, the tau-analogue of a lattice gauge configuration.

registry_objects.title: Strong curvature
registry_objects.summary: The strong curvature F_n^s(Box) at plaquette Box and stage n measures the norm of the ordered composition of connection automorphisms around an elementary closed path minus the identity, quantifying the failure of parallel transport to commute around Box.

registry_objects.title: Plaquette-aggregated strong defect
registry_objects.summary: The plaquette-aggregated strong defect V_n^s(Gamma_n) = Agg({F_n^s(Box) | Box in P_n^s}) is the canonical aggregation of strong curvatures over all plaquettes, the plaquette reformulation of the gap-loop defect functional suited to spectral analysis.

registry_objects.title: Canonical strong vacuum, plaquette form
registry_objects.summary: The canonical strong vacuum in plaquette form is Gamma_s^*[n] := argmin over V_n^s-minimizers of code_n^s(Gamma_n), the NF-coded tie-breaking among plaquette-defect minimizers, equivalent to the gap-loop construction.

registry_objects.title: Strong quadratic form
registry_objects.summary: The strong quadratic form Q_n^s(p,q) is the finite-difference second variation of V_n^s around the strong vacuum Gamma_s^*[n], analogous to the Hessian of the Yang-Mills action evaluated at the vacuum, whose eigenvalues determine the excitation spectrum.

registry_objects.title: Spectral gap at stage~n
registry_objects.summary: The spectral gap delta_n^s := lambda_1^(n) = min{lambda in Spec(Q_n^s) | lambda > 0} is the smallest nonzero eigenvalue of the strong quadratic form at stage n; the corresponding eigenmode g_n is the lightest excitation above the strong vacuum.

registry_objects.title: YM sector coupling
registry_objects.summary: The YM sector coupling mu_YM(k) is the ratio of the B-product to the C-product of the split-complex zeta function at primorial depth k (III.D46), measuring the degree of asymmetry between the two bipolar factorizations that controls the spectral gap scale.

registry_objects.title: Gap quantum
registry_objects.summary: The omega-gap quantum g[omega] := varprojlim_{n>=3} g_n is the projective limit of finite-stage gap modes; its spectral weight lambda_omega^s(g[omega]) := lim delta_n^s is the mass gap of the strong sector.

registry_objects.title: Readout functor (conjectural)
registry_objects.summary: The tau-to-orthodox readout functor R: Spec_tau(C) -> Spec_YM(SU(3)) is a conjectured map from the tau-spectrum of the C-sector to the physical spectrum of SU(3) Yang-Mills on R^4, required to preserve gaps, ordering, and multiplicities.

registry_objects.title: Orthodox Bridge Conjecture
registry_objects.summary: The Orthodox Bridge Conjecture asserts that a readout functor satisfying gap preservation, spectral ordering, and multiplicity conditions exists, so that the tau-mass gap delta_infinity^s > 0 implies a mass gap Delta > 0 in continuum SU(3) Yang-Mills on R^4.

registry_objects.title: Fluid Regime
registry_objects.summary: 8 canonical fluid regimes: Crystal, Glass, Euler, Navier-Stokes, MHD, Plasma, Superfluid, Superconductor. Classified by defect-tuple inequality patterns.

registry_objects.title: π-lift at stage n
registry_objects.summary: The pi-lift at stage n is Lift_pi(n), obtained by restricting the canonical strong lift Lift_{s,n} to pi-supported endomorphisms and selecting the NF-minimal element; it is the tau-analogue of a deep-inelastic scattering probe of the strong sector.

registry_objects.title: π-lift ω-limit
registry_objects.summary: The pi-lift omega-limit Lift_pi^omega := [(Lift_pi(n))_{n>=3}]_{~omega} in H_partial is the tail equivalence class of the finite-stage pi-lifts, representing the profinite strong coupling as a well-defined element of the boundary algebra.

registry_objects.title: The τ-strong coupling constant
registry_objects.summary: The tau-strong coupling constant alpha_s^* := NF(Lift_pi^omega) in Fix(s) is the normal-form selector applied to the pi-lift omega-limit, yielding a unique element of the boundary algebra determined entirely by the strong vacuum and pi-support constraint.

registry_objects.title: π-support penalty
registry_objects.summary: The pi-support penalty Pen_pi[n](x) := sum_{k=n+1}^{2n} ||x|_k - pr_pi(x|_k)||_{R[k]} measures how far an endomorphism deviates from pure pi-typed action at stages beyond n, penalizing non-pi-typed contamination in the strong coupling construction.

registry_objects.title: Ontic coupling
registry_objects.summary: An ontic coupling is an element of H_partial obtained by finite-stage minimization, omega-tail stabilization, and NF normalization, belonging to Fix(S) for some sector S. It is the fundamental, scale-independent quantity.

registry_objects.title: Regime selector
registry_objects.summary: A regime selector is a finite datum specifying a truncation depth n_0, an operational chart (coordinate choice on the readout target), a sector carrier choice, and a calibration bridge from tau-units to SI or MS-bar units.

registry_objects.title: Regime readout map
registry_objects.summary: The regime readout map Read_S[R]: H_partial -> R_R maps boundary algebra elements to real numbers in the metric of the regime's operational chart, extracting the measured value of an ontic coupling in a specific experimental context.

registry_objects.title: Quark mode
registry_objects.summary: A quark mode is a character mode chi_{m,n} on T^2 with eta-winding number n not equiv 0 mod 3, carrying color class c = n mod 3 in {1,2}; by the Confinement Theorem such modes cannot exist as isolated stable states.

registry_objects.title: Antiquark mode
registry_objects.summary: The antiquark of a quark mode chi_{m,n} is the conjugate mode bar{chi}_{m,n} := chi_{-m,-n}, with reversed color class bar{c} = (-n) mod 3 and reversed electric charge -Q, corresponding to the CP-conjugate character on T^2.

registry_objects.title: Quark generations from \Lemniscate
registry_objects.summary: The three quark generations arise from three topological mode classes on L: Generation 1 (u,d) = crossing-point modes, Generation 2 (c,s) = single-lobe modes, Generation 3 (t,b) = full-lemniscate modes, with increasing breathing eigenvalues.

registry_objects.title: Regime Signature
registry_objects.summary: Regime signature: structural properties distinguishing each fluid regime — mobility bound, Kelvin invariance, dissipation, EM coupling, quantized circulation, incompressibility.

registry_objects.title: Meson state
registry_objects.summary: A meson is a composite state |q bar{q}> formed from a quark mode chi_{m1,n1} and an antiquark mode chi_{-m2,-n2} such that the total color charge c_total = n1 mod 3 + (-n2) mod 3 equiv 0 mod 3 vanishes, making it a color singlet.

registry_objects.title: Baryon state
registry_objects.summary: A baryon is a composite state |q_r q_g q_b> formed from three quark modes with pairwise distinct color charges {n1 mod 3, n2 mod 3, n3 mod 3} = {0,1,2}, so the total color charge (n1+n2+n3) mod 3 = 0, carrying baryon number B = 1.

registry_objects.title: Boundary-first normalization
registry_objects.summary: A physical quantity Q satisfies boundary-first normalization if Q = eval composed with chi composed with omega-germ, factoring through the profinite omega-germ limit, a boundary character (tail-invariant endomorphism), and evaluation to tau-Idx.

registry_objects.title: Earned vs.\ unearned mode count
registry_objects.summary: An earned mode count N_n = dim(H_partial[n]|_{T^2}) < infinity is the number of independent boundary characters on T^2 at stage n; an unearned mode count is any infinite cardinal assigned to continuum degrees of freedom without profinite justification.

registry_objects.title: 9-element canonical generator set
registry_objects.summary: The canonical generator set of H_partial[omega] consists of nine elements in three groups: four sector vacuum idempotents (gravitational, weak, EM, strong), four gap quanta (one per sector), and the crossing generator iota_tau coupling chi_+ and chi_- at the lemniscate crossing point.

registry_objects.title: tau-Yukawa coupling
registry_objects.summary: The tau-Yukawa coupling of a fermion mode chi_{m,n} in sector X to the Higgs sector omega is y_f = kappa(omega) / sqrt(m^2 + n^2 iota_tau^2) times a generation factor Gamma_gen(f), determined by winding-mode overlap with the omega-sector crossing character.

registry_objects.title: Three mode classes on lemniscate
registry_objects.summary: Character modes on T^2 restricted to L = S^1 v S^1 fall into three topological mode classes: crossing-point modes (Generation 1, localized near p_omega, smallest eigenvalue), single-lobe modes (Generation 2, winding around one lobe), and full-lemniscate modes (Generation 3, winding around both lobes, largest eigenvalue).

registry_objects.title: Quark winding classes
registry_objects.summary: The six quarks are assigned to three winding classes on T^2 with shape ratio iota_tau: Class (1,0) for Generation 1 (u, d) with eigenvalue beta = 1, Class (0,1) for Generation 2 (c, s) with eigenvalue beta = iota_tau^(-1), and Class (1,1) for Generation 3 (t, b) with eigenvalue beta = iota_tau^(-2).

registry_objects.title: Koide parameter
registry_objects.summary: The Koide parameter is Q = (m_e + m_mu + m_tau) / (sqrt(m_e) + sqrt(m_mu) + sqrt(m_tau))^2, a dimensionless ratio of the three charged lepton masses discovered by Yoshio Koide in 1982, experimentally equal to 0.666661 +/- 0.000007.

registry_objects.title: Rydberg constant
registry_objects.summary: The Rydberg constant R_infinity = alpha_em^2 m_e c / (2 hbar) encodes the hydrogen energy levels via E_n = -hcR_infinity/n^2; it is a derived quantity in Category tau since both alpha_em and m_e are iota_tau-determined, making it a parameter-free prediction.

registry_objects.title: Mass Index
registry_objects.summary: Mass index: inertial invariant of persistent T² defect bundle. Boundary fixed-point of coherence functional. Monotone under admissible evolution.

registry_objects.title: Meson classification
registry_objects.summary: A meson |q_i q_bar_j> is classified by three attributes: flavor content (quark flavors from {u,d,s,c,b,t}), spin-parity J^PC (from orbital and spin angular momentum), and generation class (lemniscate mode classes of constituent quarks); pseudoscalar (J=0) and vector (J=1) mesons correspond to anti-aligned and aligned spins.

registry_objects.title: Glueball
registry_objects.summary: A glueball is a bound state of the strong vacuum field Gamma_s^* with no quark content: a color-neutral excitation of the su(3) connection field above the vacuum minimum, carrying positive mass at or above the Yang-Mills mass gap m_gap, predicted by lattice QCD at ~1.5-1.7 GeV for J^PC = 0^++.

registry_objects.title: Nuclear force
registry_objects.summary: The nuclear force between two nucleons is the residual C-sector interaction from partial overlap of their internal color fields at separations ~1 fm; at E1 readout it is mediated by virtual meson exchange, principally the pion (lightest meson, range ~ hbar/m_pi c ~ 1.4 fm).

registry_objects.title: Atom as dressed nuclear mode
registry_objects.summary: An atom of atomic number Z is a stable composite of a nuclear core (bound state of Z protons and N neutrons) and an electron shell (Z electron winding modes on T^2 bound by B-sector EM coupling); the neutral atom has vanishing net B-sector winding, making it electromagnetically closed.

registry_objects.title: Electron quantum numbers
registry_objects.summary: An electron mode on T^2 bound to a nuclear core of charge Z carries four quantum numbers: principal n (total winding depth, breathing operator eigenvalue tier), angular l = 0,...,n-1 (lobe structure on L), magnetic m_l = -l,...,+l (orientation on L), and spin m_s = +/-1/2 (chirality on T^2).

registry_objects.title: Covalent bond
registry_objects.summary: A covalent bond of order k between atoms A and B is a set of k electron winding modes on T^2 that contribute simultaneously to the shell closure of both atoms: k=1 (single bond, e.g., H_2), k=2 (double bond, e.g., O=O), k=3 (triple bond, e.g., N triple-bond N); bond strength increases with k via mode-overlap integrals.

registry_objects.title: Ionic bond
registry_objects.summary: An ionic bond is a complete transfer of electron winding modes from atom A to atom B such that both ions achieve or approach noble gas closure; the bond energy is the Coulomb interaction E_ionic ~ -k^2 alpha / r_AB, where alpha is the fine-structure constant and r_AB the inter-nuclear separation.

registry_objects.title: Metallic bond
registry_objects.summary: A metallic bond is a collective binding mode in which outermost electron winding modes are delocalized across the lattice (the T^2-winding analogue of the electron sea); delocalization explains conductivity (modes propagate under fields), malleability, and luster, arising in elements with few outer-shell electrons.

registry_objects.title: Hybrid modes
registry_objects.summary: A hybrid mode is a linear combination of s-type (l=0) and p-type (l=1) winding modes optimized for directional bonding: sp^3 yields four tetrahedral hybrids (109.5 deg, e.g., CH_4), sp^2 yields three planar hybrids plus one perpendicular p-mode (120 deg, e.g., C_2H_4), sp yields two linear hybrids (180 deg).

registry_objects.title: Ontic entity
registry_objects.summary: An entity is ontic in Category tau if it satisfies at least one of: well-defined mode on fiber T^2 (particle), well-defined mode on base tau^1 (temporal/gravitational), well-defined crossing mode at omega = gamma cap eta (Higgs-type), or finite composite of ontic modes (hadrons, nuclei, atoms).

registry_objects.title: Energy Index
registry_objects.summary: Energy index: coherence cost of maintaining localized defect bundle. Proportional to defect-tuple magnitude and stability degree. Sector-specific excitation.

registry_objects.title: Macroscopic defect tuple
registry_objects.summary: The macroscopic defect tuple in sector X for an N-bundle configuration C is D_X^macro(C) = sum_i D_X(d_i) + I_X(C), where I_X(C) is the interaction correction; the total is summed over all five sectors {D, A, B, C, omega}.

registry_objects.title: Macroscopic mobility
registry_objects.summary: Macroscopic mobility mu^macro(C) = (1/N) sum_i mu(d_i) + mu_int(C), the first component of D^macro, where the interaction term mu_int encodes collective resistance or facilitation of base-direction flow for the N-body configuration.

registry_objects.title: Macroscopic vorticity
registry_objects.summary: Macroscopic vorticity nu^macro(C) = (1/N) sum_i nu(d_i) + nu_int(C), the average rotational content plus collective circulation modes; in a superfluid nu^macro = 0 everywhere except at quantized vortex cores where topological charge concentrates.

registry_objects.title: Macroscopic compression
registry_objects.summary: Macroscopic compression kappa^macro(C) = (1/N) sum_i kappa(d_i) + kappa_int(C), measuring collective density variation; in a crystal kappa^macro approx 0 because the lattice enforces fixed density, while in a gas kappa^macro fluctuates freely.

registry_objects.title: Total topological charge
registry_objects.summary: Total topological charge theta^tot(C) = sum_i theta(d_i) is the additive, integer-valued sum of individual charges with no averaging and no interaction correction, since theta is a homotopy invariant immune to continuous deformation.

registry_objects.title: Clopen cylinder at depth n
registry_objects.summary: A clopen cylinder at primorial depth n is C_{n,a} = {x in Z-hat : x equiv a mod p_n#} for a in Z/p_n#Z; there are exactly p_n# such cylinders partitioning Z-hat, each simultaneously open and closed in the profinite topology.

registry_objects.title: Level-n defect functional
registry_objects.summary: The level-n defect functional delta_n[omega] maps clopen cylinders at depth n to R^3 x Z, assigning to each C_{n,a} the sum of defect components (mu, nu, kappa, theta) over all bundles whose addresses lie in that cylinder, plus interaction corrections.

registry_objects.title: Universal defect functional
registry_objects.summary: The universal defect functional delta[omega] = projlim_n delta_n[omega] is the projective limit in the category of finitely additive measures on the clopen algebra of Z-hat valued in R^3 x Z, assigning a defect 4-tuple to every clopen subset U of Z-hat.

registry_objects.title: Defect tuple space
registry_objects.summary: The defect tuple space is D = R_{>=0} x R x R x Z, where the four factors correspond to (mu, nu, kappa, theta): mobility is non-negative, vorticity and compression are real-valued (signed), and topological charge is integer-valued.

registry_objects.title: Critical mobility threshold
registry_objects.summary: The critical mobility threshold mu_crit is the macroscopic mobility value at which the Euler budget ceases to hold; for mu <= mu_crit the budget is conserved, while for mu > mu_crit viscous dissipation breaks the budget and entropy production becomes non-negligible.

registry_objects.title: Speed Constant
registry_objects.summary: Speed-of-light constant c²_τ: τ-derived structural constant relating mass and energy indices. Not postulated but earned from τ-kernel.

registry_objects.title: Crystal regime
registry_objects.summary: The crystal regime is the subset of D where mu < epsilon, |nu| < epsilon, |kappa| < epsilon, and theta = theta_0 (fixed integer); all three continuous components are nearly frozen and the topological charge is locked to a fixed value.

registry_objects.title: Glass regime
registry_objects.summary: The glass regime is the subset of D where mu < epsilon, |nu| < epsilon, |kappa| >= epsilon, and theta = theta_0; mobility and vorticity are frozen like a crystal, but compression remains unfrozen, allowing local density variations to persist.

registry_objects.title: Euler fluid regime
registry_objects.summary: The Euler fluid regime is the subset of D where 0 < mu <= mu_crit and the Euler budget constraint mu + nu + kappa + theta = B_0 holds; flow is inviscid with no entropy production, the tau-native analog of ideal fluid dynamics on the fiber T^2.

registry_objects.title: Navier-Stokes regime
registry_objects.summary: The Navier-Stokes regime is the subset of D where mu > mu_crit; above the critical mobility threshold the Euler budget is violated, with viscous source terms (g_mu, g_nu, g_kappa) satisfying g_mu + g_nu + g_kappa != 0.

registry_objects.title: MHD regime
registry_objects.summary: The MHD (magnetohydrodynamic) regime is the subset of D where nu >> mu and kappa is coupled to the B-sector; the system is rotating far more than translating, with compression locked to electromagnetic field gradients, describing stellar interiors and plasmas.

registry_objects.title: Plasma regime
registry_objects.summary: The plasma regime is the subset of D where mu, |nu|, |kappa| > mu_crit and theta is fluctuating (not globally fixed); topological charge varies across the configuration, representing the ionized, fully mobile state of matter.

registry_objects.title: Superfluid regime
registry_objects.summary: The superfluid regime is the subset of D where mu = mu_max, nu = 0 a.e. (vanishing vorticity except at isolated quantized vortex cores), kappa = 0 (incompressible), and theta in Z (quantized topological charge).

registry_objects.title: Superconductor regime
registry_objects.summary: The superconductor regime is the subset of D where B-sector mobility mu_B = mu_max, theta in Z (quantized), and magnetic flux Phi_B = theta * Phi_0 with flux quantum Phi_0 = hbar_tau/(2*theta_e); it combines maximal EM-sector mobility with flux quantization.

registry_objects.title: Temperature as defect gradient
registry_objects.summary: The tau-temperature T_tau(C) = d delta[omega](C) / d S_def(C) is the gradient of the universal defect functional with respect to defect entropy, a derived quantity measuring the rate of defect-functional change when defect entropy varies at fixed refinement entropy.

registry_objects.title: First-order phase transition
registry_objects.summary: A first-order phase transition at defect entropy S_0 is a discontinuity in the tau-temperature: lim_{S->S_0^-} T_tau(S) != lim_{S->S_0^+} T_tau(S), equivalently a jump discontinuity in d delta / d S_def at S_0.

registry_objects.title: Mass-Energy Relation
registry_objects.summary: E = m·c²_τ: structural identity between mass and energy indices via speed constant. Proof obligation: cross-multiplication equality on scaled rationals.

registry_objects.title: Second-order phase transition
registry_objects.summary: A second-order phase transition at S_0 is a point where T_tau is continuous but its derivative dT_tau/dS_def is discontinuous, equivalently a jump in d^2 delta / d S_def^2; examples include the superconducting transition and superfluid lambda point.

registry_objects.title: tau-Euler flow
registry_objects.summary: A tau-Euler flow is a sequence of tau-admissible configurations {d_n} satisfying: mobility bound mu(d_n) <= mu_crit, budget conservation mu_n + nu_n + kappa_n + theta_n = B_0, and propagation coherence d_{n+1} = Phi_{n,n+1}(d_n).

registry_objects.title: tau-Navier-Stokes flow
registry_objects.summary: A tau-Navier-Stokes flow is a sequence {d_n} where mu(d_n) > mu_crit for some or all n, with viscous budget decay B_{n+1} - B_n proportional to mobility excess; the Euler budget is no longer conserved and entropy production occurs from viscous dissipation.

registry_objects.title: Superfluid regime
registry_objects.summary: A tau-admissible configuration is in the superfluid regime if mu is maximal (free base-direction translation), nu = 0 except at isolated vortex cores with non-trivial winding around T^2 cycles, and kappa = 0 (incompressible bulk).

registry_objects.title: Superconductor regime
registry_objects.summary: A tau-admissible configuration is in the superconductor regime if B-sector mobility mu_B is maximal, topological charge theta_B in Z is quantized, and magnetic flux Phi_B = n*Phi_0 (n in Z) with flux quantum Phi_0 = h/(2e).

registry_objects.title: Crystal regime
registry_objects.summary: A tau-admissible configuration is in the crystal regime if mu approx 0 (atoms locked), nu approx 0 (no rotation), kappa approx 0 (rigid lattice), and theta forms a repeating periodic pattern on T^2 with coherent long-range order.

registry_objects.title: Glass regime
registry_objects.summary: A tau-admissible configuration is in the glass regime if mu approx 0 (locked), nu approx 0 (locked), kappa > 0 (compression unfrozen, local density variations persist), and theta is fixed but aperiodic (no repeating topological charge pattern).

registry_objects.title: Quasicrystal regime
registry_objects.summary: A tau-admissible configuration is in the quasicrystal regime if all four components (mu, nu, kappa, theta) are frozen and the topological charge pattern theta has incommensurate winding numbers around the two circles of T^2 (irrational ratio w_gamma/w_eta).

registry_objects.title: First-order phase transition
registry_objects.summary: A first-order phase transition (ch53 formulation) is a transition where one or more defect-tuple components undergo a discontinuous jump as a control parameter crosses an inequality boundary; examples include melting (mu jumps from ~0 to >0).

registry_objects.title: Second-order phase transition
registry_objects.summary: A second-order (continuous) phase transition is a transition where all defect-tuple components are continuous but one or more of their derivatives with respect to a control parameter diverge at the inequality boundary; examples include the normal-to-superconductor transition.

registry_objects.title: Entropy Splitting
registry_objects.summary: S = S_def + S_ref: defect entropy (→ 0 at coherence horizon) plus refinement entropy (unbounded). Second-Law Inversion: S_def reverses at horizon.

registry_objects.title: Topological branch
registry_objects.summary: A topological branch of the defect spectrum is a regime with nonzero maximal mobility, zero bulk vorticity nu_bulk = 0, and quantized topological charge theta in Z (or theta_B in Z for the B-sector branch); superfluids and superconductors live on topological branches.

registry_objects.title: Tower-natural transformation
registry_objects.summary: A tower-natural transformation eta: F => G between sector functors F, G: tau^1 -> tau^3|_{T^2} is a family {eta_n: F[n] -> G[n]} in the boundary holonomy algebra H_partial satisfying eta_{n+1} circ Phi^F = Phi^G circ eta_n for all tower levels n >= 1, encoding compatibility with propagation.

registry_objects.title: tau-sphaleron question
registry_objects.summary: The tau-sphaleron question asks whether a non-perturbative process in Category tau can change the topological winding number theta by a nonzero integer while respecting all tower-compatibility conditions and sector isolation (K5). It decomposes into sub-problems about vacuum topology, barrier height, and cross-sector coupling kappa(A,C) = iota_tau^3.

registry_objects.title: Book V import list
registry_objects.summary: Book V Import List: Book IV exports complete fiber T^2 physics, all 10 coupling constants as rational functions of iota_tau (Lean-verified), the defect functional delta[omega], the particle spectrum dictionary, the calibration anchor m_n, and five open problems (sphaleron, readout functor, dark matter, Lambda, closing identity).

registry_objects.title: Book VI import list
registry_objects.summary: Book VI Import List: Book IV exports the four-component defect tuple and universal defect functional as substrate for biological defect dynamics, the eight fluid regime classification (crystal through plasma), the particle spectrum for biochemical atoms, and the E2 computational layer preview for biological computation.

registry_objects.title: Book VII import list
registry_objects.summary: Book VII Import List: Book IV exports the ontic/non-ontic ontological framework, the self-enrichment claim that tau^3 is enriched over itself, the deterministic dynamism principle reconciling ontic determinism with address-level indeterminacy, and the ethical grounding from categorical structure -- all at the metaphorical tier.

registry_objects.title: Coherence Kernel --- Physics Presentation
registry_objects.summary: The coherence kernel K = ({alpha, pi, gamma, eta, omega}, rho, K0-K6) restated in physics language. The seven axioms from Book I Parts I-III are inherited as mathematics; the physical reading is forced by the Generator-Sector Correspondence of Book III.

registry_objects.title: Generator--Sector Assignment
registry_objects.summary: The canonical bijection sending alpha -> D (Gravity), pi -> A (Weak), gamma -> B (EM), eta -> C (Strong), omega -> H (Higgs). Respects the base-fiber decomposition: {alpha, pi} generate base tau^1, {gamma, eta} generate fiber T^2, omega couples base to fiber.

registry_objects.title: Ontic Minimality
registry_objects.summary: The coherence kernel K is ontically minimal if it satisfies sufficiency (every physical structure is derivable from K as a readout of H_partial[omega]) and necessity (no proper subset of K is sufficient -- removing any axiom or generator makes at least one readout underivable).

registry_objects.title: Refinement Tower mathcalR
registry_objects.summary: The refinement tower R = (alpha_n, rho_n)_{n >= 1} with alpha_n := rho^{n-1}(alpha) and transition maps rho_n : alpha_n -> alpha_{n+1}. A directed system forming a chain alpha_1 -> alpha_2 -> ... encoding all levels of the progression operator applied to the seed generator alpha.

registry_objects.title: Defect Budget
registry_objects.summary: Defect budget: conserved total of 4-component defect tuple in Euler regime. τ-native Kelvin circulation theorem.

registry_objects.title: Profinite Limit hatalpha
registry_objects.summary: The profinite limit hat{alpha} := varprojlim_n alpha_n is the set of coherent threads (x_1, x_2, ...) with x_n in alpha_n and rho_n(x_n) = x_{n+1}. It captures all levels simultaneously as a categorical limit in the category of directed systems, with omega as the formal boundary.

registry_objects.title: Proto-Time t_p
registry_objects.summary: Proto-time t_p(alpha_n) := n is the rho-iteration depth: the number of applications of rho needed to reach alpha_n from the seed generator alpha. Proto-time is earned from the kernel axioms, not postulated. Its properties follow from the structure of the alpha-orbit.

registry_objects.title: Base tau^1 --- physical reading
registry_objects.summary: The base tau^1 of the tau^3 fibration is the two-dimensional space generated by the outer generators alpha (radial/ultrametric direction encoding prime factorization depth) and pi (solenoidal/angular direction encoding primorial cycling). Together they span the temporal sector carrying proto-time and gravity/weak structure.

registry_objects.title: Fiber T^2 --- physical reading
registry_objects.summary: The fiber T^2 of the tau^3 fibration is the two-dimensional space generated by the inner generators gamma (second solenoidal direction, exponent coordinate) and eta (third solenoidal direction, tetration coordinate). The fiber is homogeneous at any base point, responsible for translational symmetry of spatial physics.

registry_objects.title: Fibered product arena tau^3
registry_objects.summary: The arena of all physics is the fibered product tau^3 = tau^1 x_f T^2, where the subscript f denotes that admissible fiber coordinates (B,C) depend on the base point (D,A). The coupling between base and fiber passes through the fifth generator omega.

registry_objects.title: Master constant iota_tau
registry_objects.summary: The master constant iota_tau = 2/(pi + e) approx 0.341304. The numerator 2 reflects the bipolar splitting of the lemniscate (two lobes, two idempotents). The denominator pi + e couples the temporal transcendental e (base growth) to the spatial transcendental pi (fiber periodicity).

registry_objects.title: Lemniscate boundary --- physical reading
registry_objects.summary: The boundary of tau^3 is partial(tau^3) = {omega} x_f L where L = S^1 v S^1 is the lemniscate: two circles meeting at a single point (the omega crossing). Each lobe carries one fiber generator: the chi_+-lobe hosts EM (B-coordinate), the chi_--lobe hosts Strong (C-coordinate).

registry_objects.title: Chart readout homomorphism
registry_objects.summary: The chart readout homomorphism Phi_p : H_partial[omega] -> Jet_p[omega] maps the full boundary holonomy algebra to its jet-space image at a point p in tau^3. The jet algebra Jet_p[omega] contains the Taylor data of H_partial[omega]-elements evaluated at the ABCD coordinates of p.

registry_objects.title: Yoneda self-image
registry_objects.summary: The Yoneda self-image Y_L(tau) = Nat(h^L, h^L) is the algebra of natural transformations of the representable functor h^L = Hom_tau(-, L) at the lemniscate boundary. In a self-enriched category, this lands in tau itself, making self-description a structural feature, not a metaphor.

registry_objects.title: Boundary character
registry_objects.summary: A boundary character on L is a group homomorphism chi : pi_1(L) -> U(1) assigning a phase to each homotopy class of loops. Since pi_1(L, omega) = F_2 = <a, b> (free group on two generators), the character variety is T^2, matching the fiber torus of the fibered product structure.

registry_objects.title: SI Reference Table
registry_objects.summary: SI physical constants stored as exact scaled Nat pairs. 4 exact constants (c, h, e, k_B from 2019 SI revision) plus Avogadro N_A. Structure: name, numer, denom, denom_pos, is_exact.

registry_objects.title: Bipolar decomposition of characters
registry_objects.summary: Every character on L decomposes uniquely as chi = chi_+ + chi_- under the lobe-exchange involution sigma. The sigma-invariant part chi_+ lives on the gamma-lobe (EM sector B); the sigma-anti-invariant part chi_- lives on the eta-lobe (Strong sector C). This is the bipolar spectral decomposition.

registry_objects.title: Physical-constants core
registry_objects.summary: The physical-constants core C_phys = Q(iota_tau) is the closure of the master constant iota_tau = 2/(pi + e) under field operations and sector lifts. Every physical constant is an element of C_phys. This is a single-generator field extension over the rationals.

registry_objects.title: Canonical sector lifts
registry_objects.summary: The five canonical sector lifts evaluated at iota_tau: Lift_B = iota_tau^2 (EM), Lift_A = iota_tau (Weak), Lift_C = iota_tau^3/(1 - iota_tau) (Strong), Lift_D = 1 - iota_tau (Gravity), Lift_omega = iota_tau^3/(1 + iota_tau) (Higgs). All are rational functions of one master constant.

registry_objects.title: Chart readout homomorphism
registry_objects.summary: For each point p in tau^3, the chart readout homomorphism Phi_p : H_partial[omega] -> Jet_p[omega] restricts global boundary holonomy elements to local jet data. The metric g_mu_nu, Christoffel symbols, Riemann curvature, and matter fields are all Phi_p-images of H_partial[omega] elements.

registry_objects.title: Generator--Sector Correspondence
registry_objects.summary: The Generator-Sector Correspondence is the canonical transfer map Phi : G_0 -> G_1 sending each kernel generator at E0 to its E1 sector instantiation: alpha -> D (Gravity), pi -> A (Weak), gamma -> B (EM), eta -> C (Strong), omega -> omega_H (Higgs). The 4+1 structure is forced by Object Closure (K6).

registry_objects.title: Coupling Ledger
registry_objects.summary: The coupling ledger is the symmetric 5x5 matrix of inter-sector couplings kappa(X,Y) for X, Y in {D, A, B, C, omega}. Symmetry kappa(X,Y) = kappa(Y,X) reduces to ten independent entries: five self-couplings and five cross-couplings, all rational functions of iota_tau.

registry_objects.title: Boundary holonomy generators
registry_objects.summary: The canonical generator set of H_partial[omega] consists of nine elements: four sector vacua (EM, weak, strong, gravitational ground states), four smallest excitations (photon, Higgs, gluon gap, graviton), and one crossing-point mediator (iota_tau coupling chi_+ to chi_- at the lemniscate crossing).

registry_objects.title: Defect bundle (ontic particle)
registry_objects.summary: An ontic particle is a persistent localized defect bundle d subset H_partial[omega] satisfying: (1) persistence under propagation Phi_{n,n+1} for all n >= n_0, (2) localization in a bounded T^2 address neighborhood, and (3) full fiber topology -- both circles of T^2 contribute, distinguishing massive particles from radiation.

registry_objects.title: Radiation
registry_objects.summary: A radiation mode is a persistent excitation r subset H_partial[omega] with degenerate fiber topology: the T^2 torus degenerates to S^1 with one direction collapsed. Photons and gravitons are radiation modes, massless because the collapsed fiber direction offers no resistance to base-shift.

registry_objects.title: Virtual particle
registry_objects.summary: A virtual particle is a transient defect configuration appearing at refinement level n but not persisting to level n+k for any fixed k. Virtual particles mediate interactions between ontic particles (internal lines in Feynman diagrams) but have no independent existence in H_partial[omega].

registry_objects.title: SI Measured Constants
registry_objects.summary: 9 CODATA 2022 measured constants: m_n, m_e, m_p, 1/α, sin²θ_W, α_s(M_Z), R=m_n/m_e, Δm(n-p), G. All stored as (numer, denom) Nat pairs with positive denominators.

registry_objects.title: Five primary invariants

registry_objects.title: Holomorphic Hilbert Space

registry_objects.title: Physical State Space

registry_objects.title: Entanglement

registry_objects.title: Holomorphic Vector Field

registry_objects.title: Address Uncertainty
registry_objects.summary: Position uncertainty (Δx)² and momentum uncertainty (Δp)² for a normalized state ψ ∈ H_τ, defined as expectation-value variances of X-hat and P-hat. Quantifies address precision on the fiber T².

registry_objects.title: τ-Normal Form for Joint Address

registry_objects.title: Phase Transport Witness
registry_objects.summary: The phase transport witness W_ω(f) at the lemniscate crossing point ω measures the rate at which γ-address and η-address information diverge. Defined as the derivative of the difference f|_{S¹_γ} − f|_{S¹_η} at ω.

registry_objects.title: Clopen Position Localization
registry_objects.summary: A state f ∈ H_τ is clopenly localized in position at scale ε if its γ-address distribution is supported on a clopen subset U_γ ⊂ S¹_γ of angular measure |U_γ| ≤ ε. Natural localization notion on compact profinite fiber.

registry_objects.title: σ-Equivariant Crossing-Point Mediator

registry_objects.title: Canonical Saturation State

registry_objects.title: Address Resolution
registry_objects.summary: Measurement of an observable on ψ ∈ H_τ is address resolution: coupling ψ to a device whose pointer has a definite eigenvalue, selecting a single eigenstate. No collapse axiom.

registry_objects.title: Decoherence
registry_objects.summary: Suppression of off-diagonal elements of the reduced density matrix due to entanglement with environmental degrees of freedom. Converts quantum superposition into classical mixture.

registry_objects.title: Energy as CR-Tension
registry_objects.summary: Energy of a CR-function f on τ³ is the holomorphic tension integral E[f] = ∫_{τ³} |∂̄_b f|² dμ. Measures the structural cost of maintaining a CR-compatible address.

registry_objects.title: Graph Energy Density
registry_objects.summary: At a node n of the Cayley graph, the graph energy density ρ_E(n) is the ratio of edges to vertices in expanding balls. Discrete analogue of the CR-tension integrand.

registry_objects.title: Mass as Fiber Stiffness
registry_objects.summary: Mass m_k of a mode ψ_k is the H_∞ eigenvalue evaluated via fiber curvature. Mass = how expensive the spatial address is to maintain.

registry_objects.title: Frequency as Base Circulation
registry_objects.summary: Frequency ω_k of a mode ψ_k is the H_∞ eigenvalue evaluated via base evolution. Frequency = how fast the temporal address cycles on the lemniscate boundary.

registry_objects.title: Holomorphic Entropy

registry_objects.title: Temporal Direction

registry_objects.title: Photon Mode
registry_objects.summary: The photon is the B-sector transport mode on tau^3 with degenerate fiber character (m,n)=(0,0), nontrivial base transport along tau^1, and gamma-sector membership.

registry_objects.title: U(1) Holonomy on T^2
registry_objects.summary: The U(1) holonomy of the B-sector connection A around a closed loop on T^2 is the complex phase exp(i oint A dot dl), depending only on the homotopy class of the loop.

registry_objects.title: Electric Charge

registry_objects.title: EM Principal Bundle

registry_objects.title: Local Trivialization

registry_objects.title: Transition Function

registry_objects.title: Gauge Connection
registry_objects.summary: A connection on P_EM is a U(1)-equivariant horizontal-vertical splitting of TP_EM, equivalently a u(1)-valued 1-form A satisfying equivariance conditions.

registry_objects.title: Covariant Derivative
registry_objects.summary: The covariant derivative D_mu psi = partial_mu psi - ieA_mu psi is the unique first-order operator that transforms homogeneously under gauge transformations.

registry_objects.title: Parallel Transport

registry_objects.title: Electromagnetic Field Strength

registry_objects.title: Aharonov-Bohm Phase

registry_objects.title: EM Loop Space
registry_objects.summary: The EM loop space Omega_EM(tau^3) is the space of smooth closed loops in tau^1 with U(1) holonomy map Hol: Omega_EM -> U(1).

registry_objects.title: Sigma-Equivariance
registry_objects.summary: A U(1)-valued functional Phi on the EM loop space is sigma-equivariant if Phi(sigma o gamma) = conjugate(Phi(gamma)), respecting the bipolar involution.

registry_objects.title: Wilson Loop
registry_objects.summary: The Wilson loop W(gamma) = tr Hol(gamma) is the trace of the holonomy in a given representation; for U(1) it equals the AB phase.

registry_objects.title: Non-Abelian Gauge Field

registry_objects.title: EM Gauge Bundle

registry_objects.title: EM Connection 1-Form

registry_objects.title: Wedge Holonomy

registry_objects.title: Holonomy Normalization

registry_objects.title: Photon Phase Quantum

registry_objects.title: Sigma_A-Admissibility Selects Chirality

registry_objects.title: Discrete Hessian Spectrum

registry_objects.summary: Each of the four sector vacua (Omega^*_EM, Omega^*_wk, Gamma^*_s, nabla^*_GR) is the unique minimizer of its sector's defect functional over sector-admissible endomorphisms, not a representative of a shift equivalence class. No additive freedom remains.

registry_objects.title: Nucleon mass decomposition
registry_objects.summary: The nucleon mass decomposes as m_N = E_vac + E_kin + sum m_qi, where C-sector vacuum energy (~400 MeV), quark kinetic energy (~500 MeV), and bare quark rest masses (~12 MeV) contribute roughly 42%, 57%, and 1% respectively; the vacuum and kinetic terms account for ~99% of nucleon mass.

registry_objects.title: Nuclear force saturation

registry_objects.summary: T^2-winding modes for nucleons in a nuclear potential organize into shells of approximately equal breathing eigenvalues; cumulative nucleon counts at shell closures produce the magic numbers (2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126), paralleling the electron-shell story with nuclear-scale energy gaps.

registry_objects.title: Iron peak from competing sectors
registry_objects.summary: The binding energy maximum at A ~ 56 (iron peak) results from optimal balance between C-sector (strong) binding per nucleon (saturating) and B-sector (electromagnetic) repulsion per nucleon (growing as Z^2/A^(1/3)); the crossover where Coulomb cost exceeds marginal binding gain occurs near iron-56.

registry_objects.title: Decay channels from sector admissibility
registry_objects.summary: Every radioactive decay satisfies sector admissibility constraints: color neutrality preserved (total eta-holonomy trivial mod 3), baryon number conserved, electric charge conserved (total gamma-holonomy), and energy-momentum conserved; each decay type (alpha, beta, gamma) corresponds to a specific sector-transition pattern on T^2.

registry_objects.title: Topological integrality of theta

registry_objects.title: Quantized circulation
